# audio_conversion_tool

[← Command index](README.md)

Convert Audible AAX and AA audiobooks to M4A.

## Synopsis

```
audio_conversion_tool -i <input_path> [options]
```

## Description

The only action is `AaxToM4a`. It removes Audible's DRM with FFmpeg's
`-activation_bytes` and copies the streams unchanged (`-c copy`), so there is no
re-encoding and the chapters are kept.

The input may be one `.aax`/`.aa` file or a directory. For a file, the output is `-o`,
or the input path with an `.m4a` extension. For a directory, every `.aax`/`.aa` file
in it (and in its sub-directories with `-r`) is converted into `-o`, or into the input
directory itself, as `<name>.m4a`.

Without `-k`, the activation bytes are taken from the first of these that holds an
8-hex-digit value: `audible_activation_bytes` in `[UserData.Audible]` of the
configuration, the `-f` file, the `AUDIBLE_ACTIVATION_BYTES` environment variable, and
`~/.audible_authcode`.

## Options

### Conversion

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-a, --action <AaxToM4a>` | Conversion to run. Default: `AaxToM4a`. Allowed: `AaxToM4a`. |
| `-i, --input_path <input_path>` | `.aax`/`.aa` file, or directory of them, to convert; must exist. **Required.** |
| `-o, --output_path <output_path>` | Output `.m4a` file for a file input, or output directory for a directory input; next to the input when omitted. |

### Decryption

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-k, --activation_bytes <activation_bytes>` | Audible activation bytes, 8 hex digits; skips the automatic lookup. |
| `-f, --authcode_file <authcode_file>` | File containing the activation bytes, used when the configuration has none. |

### Behavior

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-r, --recursive` | For a directory input, also convert books in its sub-directories. |
| `--overwrite` | Replace existing output files instead of skipping those books. |

### Common options

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-v, --verbose` | Enable verbose mode. |
| `-p, --pretend_run` | Do a pretend run with no permanent changes. |
| `-x, --exit_on_failure` | Enable exit on failure mode. |
| `--no-preview` | Skip the preview confirmation prompt. |

## Examples

### Convert one book, finding the activation bytes automatically

```bash
audio_conversion_tool -i "/path/to/book.aax"
```

### Convert one book to a chosen file with explicit activation bytes

```bash
audio_conversion_tool -i "/path/to/book.aax" -o "/path/to/book.m4a" -k 1a2b3c4d
```

### Convert every book in a directory

```bash
audio_conversion_tool -i "/path/to/audiobooks"
```

### Convert a directory tree, replacing earlier conversions

```bash
audio_conversion_tool -i "/path/to/audiobooks" -r --overwrite
```

### Read the activation bytes from a file

```bash
audio_conversion_tool -i "/path/to/book.aax" -f "/path/to/authcode.txt"
```

### List what would be converted without running FFmpeg

```bash
audio_conversion_tool -i "/path/to/audiobooks" -r -p -v
```

## Notes

- Without `--overwrite`, a book whose output already exists is skipped and counted as a success.
- Needs FFmpeg.
